title: Chip-scale power delivery for kilowatt packages
bottleneck: AI packages now exceed a kilowatt, demanding enormous current at ~1V with tight regulation; resistive losses in delivery networks waste power as heat before it reaches transistors. Vertical power delivery, on-package voltage regulators, and high-current connectors add cost and complexity, and transient response to bursty AI workloads causes voltage droop. Power delivery, not logic, increasingly sets package limits.
why_it_blocks: Every watt lost in delivery is a watt stolen from compute and added to cooling load; at kilowatt scale, delivery inefficiency directly caps achievable AI throughput per rack. Data-center power provisioning becomes the binding constraint on AI scaling.
current_state: Backside power delivery, integrated voltage regulators, and 48V-to-point-of-load architectures are rolling out in flagship products. Delivering clean multi-kiloamp power at sub-1V with high efficiency remains an active engineering frontier.
